audits.title: A multi-district audit of the management of syphilis in genitourinary medicine clinics in Yorkshire.
audits.standard: National standards and guidelines for syphilis management
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine clinics across several districts in Yorkshire

cycle1.result: Satisfactory serological endpoints for about two-thirds of treated early and under one-third of treated late syphilis; HIV testing in under half of cases.

audits.other_findings: Procaine penicillin dose and duration for asymptomatic late syphilis without lumbar puncture appeared inadequate against newer guidelines.
audits.citation: McClean H, Evans A, Yorkshire Multi-District Genitourinary Medicine Clinical Audit Group. A multi-district audit of the management of syphilis in genitourinary medicine clinics in Yorkshire. Int J STD AIDS. 2004;15(3):183-188. doi:10.1258/095646204322916632. PMID: 15038865.

audits.title: Audit of the management of early syphilis at North Manchester General Hospital.
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine department, North Manchester General Hospital

cycle1.result: Treatment followed national guidelines in 63% of cases; 78% treated with intramuscular penicillin.

audits.other_findings: Only 4% of identified sexual contacts were traced and screened; adherence improved as the outbreak continued.
audits.citation: Kingston MA, Higgins SP. Audit of the management of early syphilis at North Manchester General Hospital. Int J STD AIDS. 2004;15(5):352-354. doi:10.1177/095646240401500516. PMID: 15117508.

audits.title: UK National Audit of Early Syphilis Management. Clinics audit: screening for and management of early syphilis.
audits.standard: UK national guidelines for early syphilis screening and management
audits.setting: 131 genitourinary medicine clinics in the UK (national clinics audit)

cycle1.result: 3 clinics (2%) did not routinely screen new patients and 28 (21%) did not screen rebook patients with a new partner; 19 (14%) did not routinely use recommended regimens; 7 (5%) used inferior PPG treatment.

audits.other_findings: Chest radiography was done by only 50% and lumbar puncture by 13%; audit of policies overestimated performance compared with outcomes.
audits.citation: McClean H, Daniels D, Carne C, Bunting P, Miller R, National Audit Group of the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV. UK National Audit of Early Syphilis Management. Clinics audit: screening for and management of early syphilis. Int J STD AIDS. 2006;17(5):344-348. doi:10.1258/095646206776790204. PMID: 16643686.

audits.title: UK National Audit of Early Syphilis Management. Case notes audit: diagnosis and treatment.
audits.standard: UK National Guidelines for early syphilis diagnosis and treatment
audits.setting: UK genitourinary medicine clinics (national case notes audit through Regional Audit Groups)

cycle1.result: EIA used to diagnose 695 (89%); dark ground microscopy in only 80 (29%) primary cases; HIV testing uptake 77%; 14 (5%) PPG treatments below the recommended 750 mg dose; recommended doxycycline regimen used in 104 (53%) oral treatments.

audits.other_findings: 14 (2%) cases were not treated; wide regional variation in practice.
audits.citation: McClean H, Daniels D, Carne C, Bunting P, Miller R, National Audit Group of the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV. UK National Audit of Early Syphilis Management. Case notes audit: diagnosis and treatment. Int J STD AIDS. 2006;17(5):334-339. doi:10.1258/095646206776790150. PMID: 16724418.

audits.title: UK National Audit of Early Syphilis Management. Case-notes audit: contact tracing, information giving, follow-up and outcomes.
audits.standard: UK National Guidelines: at least 60% of traceable contacts seen; follow-up at 1, 2, 3, 6 and 12 months
audits.setting: UK genitourinary medicine clinics (national case notes audit)

cycle1.result: Contact tracing provided for 683/781 (87%); 511 of 997 traceable contacts (51%) seen against a 60% standard; only 16 (2%) had follow-up at the recommended intervals.

audits.other_findings: 419/764 (55%) had a four-fold titre fall within 3-6 months; only 312 (40%) attended at least two follow-up visits.
audits.citation: McClean H, Daniels D, Carne C, Bunting P, Miller R, National Audit Group of the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV. UK National Audit of Early Syphilis Management. Case-notes audit: contact tracing, information giving, follow-up and outcomes. Int J STD AIDS. 2006;17(5):340-343. doi:10.1258/095646206776790187. PMID: 16724419.

audits.title: Audit of syphilis treatment, follow-up and contact-tracing rates.
audits.setting: Edinburgh genitourinary medicine clinic, NHS Lothian

cycle1.result: Treatment rate 100%; 90% offered testing for other STIs (positivity 24%); HIV testing rate 85%.

audits.other_findings: HIV testing led to five new diagnoses.
audits.citation: Fernando I, Thompson C. Audit of syphilis treatment, follow-up and contact-tracing rates. Int J STD AIDS. 2007;18(2):128-129. doi:10.1258/095646207779949556. PMID: 17331289.

audits.title: Audit of early syphilis: Teesside experience 2005-2007.
audits.standard: National standards for syphilis treatment, follow-up and partner notification
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine clinics in Teesside, James Cook University Hospital

cycle1.result: Treatment rate 100%; 75 of 80 had benzathine penicillin; 87 of 115 contactable partners (75.7%) screened and/or treated; satisfactory titre decline in 56 of 59 (94.9%).

audits.other_findings: 21 patients had incomplete serological follow-up; 12 of 27 females (44%) were diagnosed antenatally.
audits.citation: Tayal S, Ahmed MS, Hanif U. Audit of early syphilis: Teesside experience 2005-2007. Int J STD AIDS. 2009;20(9):647-649. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2009.009024. PMID: 19710341.

audits.title: An audit of patients treated for syphilis at Auckland Sexual Health Service.
audits.standard: Auckland Sexual Health Service treatment guidelines

cycle1.result: Care achieving acceptable outcomes; 9 (8%) had HIV infection.

audits.other_findings: Criteria for diagnosing infectious syphilis need standardising; MSM much more likely to have infectious syphilis.
audits.citation: Azariah S. An audit of patients treated for syphilis at Auckland Sexual Health Service. N Z Med J. 2010;123(1315):55-64. PMID: 20581931.

audits.title: Effective use of an audit tool devised to optimize the management of syphilis in an integrated sexual health clinic.
audits.standard: BASHH syphilis guideline auditable outcomes (baseline VDRL 100%; treatment completion 95%; contacts attending 60%)
audits.setting: Integrated sexual health clinic, Cardiff Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: All patients had baseline VDRL (target 100%); 97% completed treatment (target 95%); 100% of contactable partners attended (target 60%); 50 (60%) showed response to treatment.

audits.other_findings: 19 (23%) failed to return for follow-up VDRL. A departmental TIC proforma completed at diagnosis facilitated the audit.
audits.citation: Knapper C, Furness L, Collett M, Lomax N, Browning M. Effective use of an audit tool devised to optimize the management of syphilis in an integrated sexual health clinic. Int J STD AIDS. 2011;22(5):290-291. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2011.010392. PMID: 21571980.

audits.title: Audit of the management of the syphilis outbreak in Herefordshire 2011-2013.
audits.setting: Sexual health services, Herefordshire (Wye Valley NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: All standards for monitoring and treatment were met; contact tracing standard narrowly missed.

audits.other_findings: 88% MSM; outreach testing and contact tracing hard in rural areas.
audits.citation: Cox JH, Elliott E, Sivaprakasam V, Chima-Okereke C. Audit of the management of the syphilis outbreak in Herefordshire 2011-2013. Int J STD AIDS. 2015;26(5):357-359. doi:10.1177/0956462414538771. PMID: 24912537.
